summary: Dynamically controlled strong coupling between a superconducting SNAIL coupler and a rare-earth spin ensemble ($\mathrm{Yb}^{171}_{3+}$:YSO) was demonstrated using parametric pumping, achieving MHz-scale on-demand coupling to enable quantum state transfer. Simulations predict $\geq 98\%$ fidelity single-excitation swaps in $\sim 200$ ns, paving the way for hybrid quantum memories with coherence times ($\sim 10$ ms for spins versus $\sim 1$ ms for superconducting qubits) surpassing circuit-alone storage.
motivation: Superconducting processors suffer from limited coherence (millisecond timescale), while solid-state spin ensembles offer hours-long coherence times. Efficient quantum state transfer between circuits and spins requires dynamically tunable strong coupling, which has not been previously demonstrated despite static strong coupling being observed.
method: A 3D cavity architecture integrated a nonlinear SNAIL element capacitively coupled to a microwave bus cavity inductively coupled to a Yb$^{171}$ spin ensemble ($10$ ppm doped in Y$_2$SiO$_5$). A parametric pump applied to the SNAIL at the cavity-spin difference frequency ($\approx 10$ MHz detuning from the clock transition at $2.87$ GHz) mediated beamsplitter interactions, with coupling strength $g_{\mathrm{pump}} \propto \xi g_3$ where $\xi$ is pump amplitude and $g_3$ is the SNAIL third-order nonlinearity.
result: Normal-mode splittings confirmed strong coupling with parametric SNAIL-cavity coupling reaching several MHz linearly with pump power, and parametric SNAIL-spin coupling exceeding the static cavity-spin coupling ($1.1$ MHz) at high pump power. The apparent saturation of observed spin coupling at $1$ MHz was explained by cavity dressing; correcting for this revealed true parametric coupling of order MHz, enabling the projected fast swap timescales.
